findings:
## Issues (ranked)

1. [HIGH] The orphan rule is blind to any non-[OK] behaviour whose description contains `[OK]`.
   `scripts/check_spec_build_order_shape.py:145`: `if not OK_TAG_RE.search(joined)` searches the whole
   block, description included. `pipeline.build-order-shape` [MISSING] says "a non-[OK] behaviour" on its
   second line (spec line 86), so the guard counts it as OK. Proof: in the real spec, set to APPROVED, I
   replaced Step 1.2's `pipeline.build-order-shape` with an id that doesn't exist. The guard printed `[]`.
   Of the 42 behaviour lines, it saw 28 non-OK: 12 are [OK], 1 is [PROPOSED] (correctly left out by the
   ruling at spec line 590), and 1 is this miss.
   Fix: classify by the FIRST tag in the block, e.g.
   `TAG_RE = r"\[(OK|BROKEN|GAP|PARTIAL|MISSING|PROPOSED)[^\]]*\]"`. Take `TAG_RE.search(joined)`, and the
   behaviour is non-OK when `group(1) not in ("OK", "PROPOSED")`. Add a test whose [MISSING] behaviour
   says "non-[OK]" in its text and is in no step, so it must fail.

2. [HIGH] Wrong base. 74e3bf578's parent is c3eb829c3 (cand17 / origin/integration), not
   `pipeline/runner-v1`. That tree has neither `harness/deterministic-conductor.md` nor the `_TEMPLATE.md`
   Build order section. So the coder never ran the guard on the spec it implements: "0 build orders"
   looked green. Merging the branch as it stands would also carry 8 cand17 files into the runner branch.
   It cherry-picks cleanly onto cd1e8fd77.
   Fix: rebase the item onto runner-v1 (or cherry-pick it). Runner side: a worktree for a step of a spec
   that isn't on integration yet should be cut from the spec's branch, or the ready check should fail
   when the step's spec is absent from the tree.

3. [MED] An APPROVED spec with a `## Build order` section but zero steps that parse passes silently.
   `:157-161` and `:211-212` treat that as "no build order". So `### Step 1.1` (wrong heading level) or the
   old `Slice` headings make the whole section invisible. source-model.md and undo-everywhere.md already
   have build orders in older shapes that read as 0 steps.
   Fix: if `SECTION_RE` matched and there are 0 steps, raise a problem ("Build order has no `#### Step N.M`
   headings"). That is fail for APPROVED and warn for DRAFT, the same as the other rules.

4. [MED] Spec acceptance not delivered. (a) "the self-test parses `source/source-model.md`'s slices and
   reports the distance" (spec line 90): not done. (b) Step 1.2's Tests line names
   `pipeline/tests/test_specs.py::test_build_order_parses` and `::test_build_order_guard_fails_on_orphan_behaviour`:
   not written. Fix: write both pipeline tests (they can import the guard), and add the source-model report
   as a warning-only print in `--self-test`. Or change the spec in the same item. Don't leave it silent.

5. [MED] Four rules have no test: no Behaviours, no Tests, Size L, >5 behaviours, and Depends-on unknown.
   All five fire when probed by hand. Nothing would catch a regression in them.
   Fix: one fixture that breaks all five, then assert each message (about 15 lines).

6. [LOW] `_non_ok_behaviours` scans every `- \`id\` [TAG]` bullet in the file, Rulings and notes included
   (`:132-149`). A ruling bullet that quotes an id with a tag becomes a phantom behaviour, or a duplicate
   problem line. Fix: limit the scan to the `## Behaviours` section, or dedupe by id.

7. [LOW] `APPROVED_RE` matches anywhere in the file (`:52`), which its own ponytail comment admits. The
   Dev Pipeline spec quotes "APPROVED" in prose, though not in bold today. Fix: search only the first 20
   lines. That is one slice, and it removes the comment too.
